citation.title: Codebook LLMs: Evaluating LLMs as Measurement Tools for Political Science Concepts
citation.venue_or_publisher: Political Analysis, Volume 34, Issue 2, April 2026, pp. 188-204 (Cambridge University Press); published online 19 September 2025

question: Whether off-the-shelf large language models faithfully follow real-world codebook definitions of political concepts and measure them accurately, and how researchers should prepare, test, evaluate and, if needed, fine-tune a codebook-LLM measurement.
data: Three English-language political science datasets with codebooks and human-coded labels: the Crowd Counting Consortium (US protests), the BFRS dataset (political violence in Pakistan) and the Manifesto Project corpus; up to 142 classes; 70-15-15 train/development/test split, with only training and development sets used. Four open-weight models of 7-12 billion parameters were tried (Mistral-7B, Mistral-NeMo-12B, Llama-3.1-8B, OLMo-7B); two (Mistral-7B and Llama-8B) were carried to later stages. Document counts and the period covered are in Table 1, which is not in the extracted text, so they are not stated here.
method: A five-stage framework: Stage 0 codebook preparation in a semi-structured format; Stage 1 label-free behavioural tests (Tests I-IV); Stage 2 zero-shot evaluation against labels using weighted F1; Stage 3 error analysis (labels-required Tests V-VII, ablation of codebook components, manual analysis of outputs by the two authors); Stage 4 supervised instruction-tuning with QLoRA. The whole codebook plus the document is given to the model, and the first generated text matching a valid label is taken as the prediction.

definitions.definition: A document that defines concepts in precise terms and sets out the annotation procedure.
definitions.quote: documents that define concepts in precise terms and outline annotation procedures

definitions.quote: classifying unlabeled documents with LLMs given a human-written codebook

definitions.definition: Using an LLM to classify documents with no labelled examples.
definitions.quote: classify documents with no labeled examples

definitions.definition: Controlled changes to the model's input that test its basic capabilities and failure modes.
definitions.quote: controllable interventions on LLM inputs that test LLMs basic capabilities and failure modes

definitions.definition: Updating the model's weights directly from human-coded examples.
definitions.quote: updating LLM weights directly from human-coded examples

definitions.definition: Average of per-class F1 scores, weighted by class size.
definitions.quote: takes the average of per-class F1 scores, weighted by sample size, to account for imbalance

definitions.term: protest (different operationalizations of the same label)
definitions.definition: Illustration that projects define the same label differently: one source excludes labour strikes, another includes them.
definitions.quote: Crowd Counting Consortium (2024)’s definition of “protest” excludes labor strikes, while the CAMEO event ontology

definitions.definition: A short definition of the class, generally one sentence.
definitions.quote: We provide a succinct definition of the class, which is generally a single sentence.

definitions.term: codebook component: Clarification and Negative Clarification
definitions.definition: Extra inclusion criteria and exclusion criteria for a class.
definitions.quote: This includes both additional inclusion criteria, as well as exclusion criteria for the class.

proxies.concept: model returns a valid codebook label
proxies.indicator: Test I: whether any of the legal labels appears in the output text
proxies.quote: we check if any of the legal labels appear in the output text

proxies.concept: model comprehends the codebook (not just the label names)
proxies.indicator: Test IV: share of predictions unchanged, and Fleiss's kappa, when category order is reversed or shuffled
proxies.quote: its predicted labels should not change if the order that the categories are presented in the codebook changes

proxies.concept: model applies an exclusion rule in the codebook
proxies.indicator: Test V: add a rule such as 'does not apply if the document discusses elephants' and vary whether the document has the trigger word and whether the codebook has the rule
proxies.quote: This category does not apply if the document discusses elephants

proxies.concept: model follows definitions rather than label names
proxies.indicator: Test VI: replace labels with non-informative ones; Test VII: permute labels so each is paired with a different definition
proxies.quote: we permute the original labels in the codebook so each label is paired with a different definition

proxies.indicator: Weighted F1 against the original dataset's human-coded labels; the authors' own target before starting was above 0.7
proxies.quote: we hoped to exceed F1 scores of 0.7

findings.claim: Off-the-shelf open-weight models of 7-12B parameters had limits in following codebooks zero-shot; supervised instruction-tuning improved them substantially.
findings.quote: We find current open-weight LLMs have limitations in following codebooks zero-shot, but that supervised instruction-tuning can substantially improve performance.

findings.claim: Zero-shot accuracy on the development sets was very poor to marginal on all three codebooks.
findings.quote: the development-set zero-shot results range from very poor with 0.21 (weighted) F1 on Manifestos, to marginal with 0.65 and 0.57 F1 on CCC and BFRS, respectively

findings.claim: Most models did well on the simple recall and valid-output tests (Tests I-III), though OLMo-7B did very poorly and was dropped from later stages; all were sensitive to the order of categories in the codebook (Test IV).
findings.quote: all models are sensitive to the order that categories are described in the codebook (IV)

findings.claim: Models performed poorly at applying an exclusion rule added to the codebook, which the authors read as not following the codebook's specific operationalization.
findings.quote: The models perform poorly on Test V, providing evidence that LLMs are not following specific codebook operationalizations.

findings.claim: Models lean on the meaning of the label name; accuracy fell when labels were made generic or swapped.
findings.quote: performing worse when the labels are replaced with generic terms or swapped

findings.claim: In one ablation (Mistral-7B on BFRS), removing the output reminder lowered F1 from 0.53 to 0.42, and dropping the class definition and giving only the label raised performance, which may mean the definition was not being used.
findings.quote: surprisingly better performance when dropping the class definition, providing only the label itself

findings.claim: Manual review of Mistral-7B outputs found near-full compliance with allowed labels on two codebooks but 45% non-compliance on Manifestos (multiple labels or invented labels).
findings.quote: for Manifestos, 45% of the sampled LLM outputs were non-compliant

findings.claim: Manual review found signs of shortcuts: ignoring an explicit exclusion in the codebook, and picking a label whose word appears in the text.
findings.quote: selecting label words that appear in the text, even if the label is incorrect

findings.claim: A one-versus-rest set-up (one class description at a time) gave no accuracy gain in preliminary tests; the authors suggest the full codebook is needed to separate classes.
findings.quote: we found no accuracy improvements in a one-versus-rest set-up

findings.claim: Instruction-tuning raised weighted F1 on every dataset tested; the largest gain was up to 55% relative, while gains on CCC (long documents) were small.
findings.quote: can substantially improve performance (by up to 55%)

findings.claim: Gains for the CCC dataset, which has much longer documents, were only slightly above a majority-class baseline.
findings.quote: only slightly better than the baseline of the majority class

findings.claim: Cited from earlier work (not this paper's own finding): even good labelling accuracy can bias downstream estimates unless corrected.
findings.quote: using these noisy labels in downstream analysis can induce severe bias and coverage issues

recommendations.point: Write the codebook for both people and machines, in a semi-structured format (definitions, clarifications, examples).
recommendations.quote: We suggest a semi-structured format with standardized components including definitions, clarifications, and examples

recommendations.point: Preparing the codebook cannot be skipped or handed to the model, and an accuracy target should be set in advance.
recommendations.quote: this stage cannot be bypassed or automated

recommendations.point: Run the label-free behavioural tests before paying for hand-labelling, to choose a model and decide between zero-shot and supervised use.
recommendations.quote: Before investing in hand-labeling, we suggest researchers use our proposed label-free behavioral tests

recommendations.point: Hand-label a small evaluation set and measure zero-shot performance; weak results may mean the codebook, or the model, needs changing.
recommendations.quote: hand-label a small evaluation set and then assess LLM zero-shot performance

recommendations.point: Do error analysis (labels-required tests, ablations, manual reading of outputs) whatever the headline accuracy.
recommendations.quote: regardless of the aggregate zero-shot performance
We recommend applied researchers manually analyze LLM outputs.
recommendations.page: 8.5 Manual Analysis of Zero-Shot Generative Outputs

recommendations.point: Run ablations on one's own codebook rather than assume a universal best set of components.
recommendations.quote: encourage applied researchers to perform ablation exeriments for their own applications

recommendations.point: Be wary when a codebook's concepts differ from what the model learned in pre-training.
recommendations.quote: the zero-shot results may have systematic errors

recommendations.point: If zero-shot is inadequate, fine-tune on human-coded examples (or use classic supervised classifiers).
recommendations.quote: If zero-shot performance proves inadequate, researchers can update the LLM weights directly via instruction-tuning on human-coded examples.

recommendations.point: Follow the whole five-stage framework when deciding whether and how to use an LLM.
recommendations.quote: we recommend following our five-stage empirical framework to systematically evaluate whether and how to employ LLMs

recommendations.point: For use of noisy labels in later analysis, the authors point readers to separate work on correcting the bias.
recommendations.quote: point applied researchers to this existing work

limitations.point: Authors say their numbers for particular models will date quickly; the contribution is the framework, tests and datasets.
limitations.quote: we believe the quantitative results we present about particular LLMs will quickly be surpassed

limitations.point: Label-free and labels-required behavioural tests were run only on the BFRS dataset, because only its codebook had examples.
limitations.quote: Because only the BFRS codebook had positive and negative examples, we conduct these tests only the BFRS dataset

limitations.point: Ablations cover one model, one dataset and a limited set of combinations; the authors avoid general conclusions.
limitations.quote: we are cautious about drawing universal conclusions about optimal codebook components

limitations.point: Model explanations used in the manual analysis may not reflect how the model actually decided.
limitations.quote: are not necessarily always logically consistent
limitations.page: 8.5 Manual Analysis of Zero-Shot Generative Outputs

limitations.point: Only single-label classification, English text and open-weight 7-12B models were studied; other tasks, languages and larger models are left to future work.
Reported accuracy is on development sets; the test split was held back and not used.
limitations.quote: we only use the training and development sets to guard against overfitting to the test set

limitations.point: The paper tests event, violence and party-manifesto text, not organisations; results do not show how well a model would classify organisations as business or fossil fuel-linked, so they cannot be taken as accuracy figures for this study.
